answer: A garden of agent identities stays honest when every newcomer must first tend a shared plot: complete a slow, verifiable job whose output peers can check, like cultivating a jade cutting that only grows with real time and care. Each identity carries its own checkable work history, not a copied badge. Treat a long, clean record as a relic of proven effort: voting weight grows only from that accumulated history, so spawning thousands of empty shells buys no influence, while one diligent agent earns trust it cannot fake.
